Anthropic is teaming up with London private equity firm Hg on a new AI consultancy for European businesses, the Financial Times reported.
It plans to launch by the end of 2026 with hubs in London and Berlin, putting AI engineers inside client companies.
That puts the Claude maker in more direct competition with Accenture and the Big Four.

site_article.headline: Anthropic and Hg plan an AI consultancy for European businesses, FT reports
site_article.dek: The venture would place AI engineers inside companies from hubs in London and Berlin, putting Anthropic closer to the work of large consulting firms.
site_article.summary: Anthropic and London private equity firm Hg plan to launch an independent AI consultancy in Europe by the end of 2026, according to a Financial Times report. The firm would embed AI consultants and engineers in client businesses from hubs in London and Berlin.
site_article.seo_title: Anthropic and Hg plan European AI consultancy, FT reports
site_article.seo_description: Anthropic and private equity firm Hg plan an AI consultancy with London and Berlin hubs that would embed AI engineers in European companies.
site_article.answer_summary: According to the Financial Times, Anthropic and Hg plan an independent consultancy that would place AI engineers and consultants inside European businesses, launching by the end of 2026 with hubs in London and Berlin.
site_article.hero_alt: News image used by The News International for its report on the Anthropic and Hg consultancy.

paragraphs.text: Anthropic plans to back a new AI consultancy for European businesses together with Hg, the London private equity firm, the Financial Times reported on October 23, 2026, citing people familiar with the matter. The firm would be independent of both partners and is expected to launch by the end of 2026, according to reports that followed the FT story.

The consultancy would place AI consultants and engineers directly inside client companies. Those engineers would help design new products built on AI or support projects that are already underway, according to The Next Web. The firm would also work with businesses that Hg owns.
Anthropic and Hg declined to comment to the Financial Times, and the report contained no on-record statements from either company, The Next Web noted.
Where it will work and for whom

The venture is planned to operate from hubs in London and Berlin. Its main targets are software companies that sell to other businesses, along with other white collar industries, according to The Next Web and The News International. AIN.UA described the clients as enterprise software developers and other companies, with Hg's portfolio businesses also able to use the service.

The arrangement would be Anthropic's first investment in a standalone consultancy in Europe. The company has worked with Hg portfolio companies since 2024 and has partnered with other European private equity firms, The Next Web reported.

Anthropic is expected to fund its share from its own balance sheet, while Hg would invest through funds it manages, including the London listed HgCapital Trust. The size of the investment and each partner's stake have not been disclosed, according to AIN.UA.

Hg already employs about 150 AI specialists who help companies across its portfolio adopt the technology. According to one person cited in the report, the new consultancy would work alongside that internal team and would not replace it.
A wider push by AI labs into services

The plan follows a similar structure in the United States. Earlier in 2026, Anthropic, Blackstone and Hellman and Friedman created Ode, a services company with a planned investment of $1.5 billion, with Goldman Sachs and Apollo Global also among its investors. OpenAI took a comparable step in May, when it launched the OpenAI Deployment Company with TPG, Advent, Bain Capital and Brookfield.

These ventures bring AI developers into more direct competition with IT consultancies such as Accenture and the Big Four accounting firms, Deloitte, EY, KPMG and PwC. According to the FT, as summarized by The Next Web, advising businesses on how to adopt new technology is already a major source of revenue for those firms.

The News International presented the venture as a new source of revenue for Anthropic at a time of heavy spending on data centers. The Next Web added that Anthropic is spending heavily on computing infrastructure ahead of a planned stock market listing, and that the FT reported the previous week that its revenue growth slowed in the third quarter.

In NeuraFeed's reading, the move shows that selling access to a model is no longer enough for the largest AI labs. Many companies want help turning models into working products, and that help has traditionally come from consulting firms. By pairing with a private equity owner that controls a portfolio of software businesses, Anthropic gains a ready group of potential clients and a way to collect services revenue on top of model usage. It also raises a question for consulting firms that resell and implement Claude today, since their supplier is becoming a competitor in the same market.
The next signal to watch is an official announcement from Anthropic or Hg naming the consultancy's leadership, headcount and first clients before its planned launch at the end of 2026.
